## Documented inputs and source details

> The Innovation Adaptive Kalman Filter (IAKF) is a modern implementation of the Kalman filter that uses its own prediction errors to detect abnormal measurements and adapt its measurement-noise estimate.

> Traditionally, a Kalman filter balances its predictions and observations using predefined noise assumptions that require careful calibration. More recent research has shown how the filter can use its own prediction errors to detect abnormal measurements and adapt its measurement-noise estimate [1]. In self-driving vehicle navigation, this helps reduce the influence of disturbed GPS measurements and limit positioning errors.

> The TradingView community is also no stranger to Kalman filtering. There is already a wide variety of implementations, including price smoothers, trend overlays, oscillators, volume tools, and adaptive bands. In our review of 100 TradingView publications, nine clusters emerged based on similarities in their technical descriptions, as shown in Figure 3. Representative examples include CRYPTIK1’s Algorithmic Kalman Filter, a conventional price smoother with fixed noise settings, and Zeiierman’s Trend Strength Oscillator, which offers optional adjustments based on volume or price range.

> Misses below the threshold: The forecast errors increase, but no error is large enough for the filter to flag the bar as an outlier. No dots appear, and damping stays at zero in this example. Only the blue meter value increases. The filter continues to follow the price changes.

> Single outlier: In this example, one bar crosses the Unusual-Move Threshold. The filter flags the bar as an outlier and marks its candle. The gray curve moves down as the filter reduces its response to the price change. The blue meter remains relatively low because forecast errors on nearby bars are calm. The filter treats this bar as a single unusual event.

## Documented inputs and source details

> FlowScope: Uncover the Market's True Intent 🔬

> Group Candles: The number of standard chart candles you want to combine into a single FlowScope profile. A setting of 1 will analyze every single bar. A higher number gives you a broader market view. When Group Candles is set to 5, the data from the 5 individual candles are combined, and the volume is calculated accordingly.

> Adaptive Sizing (The Ideal Goal): FlowScope first tries to create the perfect profile by making each volume box's height proportional to the current market volatility. It calculates an "ideal" box height based on the Average True Range (ATR / 10). This is powerful because it automatically adapts: you get smaller, more detailed boxes in quiet, low-volatility markets, and larger, clearer boxes in volatile, fast-moving markets.

> Instead of just looking at the open, high, low, and close, FlowScope lets you dive deeper into the market's auction process. It groups candles together and builds a detailed Volume Profile for that period, showing you exactly where the trading happened and revealing the story behind the price action.

> Only can be used for Daily timeframe and below due to bar_time is based on minutes by default.

> Take Profit is calculated based on ratio 0.382 and 0.618 of Point A to D.

> Harmonic Patterns values is pretty much summarized here including Stop Loss.

> Length of XABCD is equal to XAB plus BCD, where XAB and BCD are one to one ratio. Length is measured in time.

> This indicator displays the Commitment of Traders (​COT) legacy data for futures markets.

> Possible values are: All, Old, Other. When commodities have a well-defined marketing season or crop year (e.g. Wheat or Lean Hogs futures), this determines how the data is aggregated. Detailed explanation can be found in the "Old and Other Futures" section of the CTFC Explanatory Notes linked above. The "Major Markets for Which the COT Data Is Shown by Crop Year" table in the Explanatory Notes specifies the commodities that this distinction applies to; selecting "Old" for any of the commodities not in that list will return the same data as in "All", while selecting "Other" will return 0.

> By default, the indicator uses the chart's symbol to derive the COT data it displays. You can also specify a CFTC code in the "CFTC code" field of the script's inputs to display COT data from a symbol different than the chart's.

> The rest of this section documents the script's input fields.

> Commitment of Traders ​(​COT) data is tallied by the Commodity ​Futures Trading Commission (CFTC), a US federal agency that oversees the trading of derivative markets such as futures in the US. It is weekly data that provides traders with information about open interest for an asset. The CFTC oversees derivative markets traded on different exchanges, so ​COT data is available for assets that can be traded on CBOT, ​CME, NYMEX, COMEX, and ICEUS.

> First of all - let me clearly state that this is solely a EDUCATIONAL IDEA & not a short recommendation - Shorting parabolic bull markets is not recommended especially for beginners and this idea is solely to give you a understanding of what A POTENTIAL blow off top can look like. If you want to show your appreciation for the insight - then i would greatly appreciate if you give the idea a like & comment thank you!

> The Bump And Run Reversal Top (BARR Top) is not a well known pattern and can be hard to identify. Price has a strong uptrend off in two phases - the bump & the run, first a small increase then recovery occurs, then price increases with massive volume at a very sharp angle. Price then makes a sharp peak and comes down breaking the support line (A); the angle of this support line is usually around a 35-50 degrees. It often throws back and bearish retests off that previous support (this is the entry point, B), its common for this rejection to be at the 0.618 Fibonacci level.

> If the downtrend breakout occurs, we can draw a measurement area from the two Swing Low (LH) points at the beginning of the BARR TOP or we can use Supply & Demand Areas to identify potential take profit or support areas. Whether you're tracking short-term fluctuations or long-term trends, Ehlers Loops can help you stay ahead of the market by offering key insights into the relationship between price and volume.

> This script implements concepts from a short-term ETF investment strategy outlined by Markos Katsanos in the article "Selecting Strong ETFs While Avoiding Sharp Overbought Reversals" from the October 2026 edition of TASC Traders' Tips. The strategy analyzes Katsanos' custom relative strength indicator, RSMK, alongside momentum and correlation to identify entry and exit conditions across a diverse set of ETFs. This script is an indicator designed for scanning for the strategy's conditions in the Pine Screener.

> Katsanos' strategy scans a diverse set of exchange-traded funds (ETFs) for strict entry and exit criteria based on relative strength, momentum, and correlation with a benchmark index. The objective is to achieve returns comparable to a buy-and-hold portfolio, while reducing downside risks for better risk-adjusted performance. The strategy operates on ETFs because they're well-suited for short-term investing. Their diversified holdings offer broad market exposure, and often high liquidity and relatively lower volatility.

> At its core, the strategy uses a modified relative strength indicator named RSMK, which Katsanos originally introduced in the March 2020 issue of TASC Traders' Tips. His RSMK aims to address the shortcomings of traditional relative strength (RS) analysis. While traditional RS calculates the ratio between two instruments' prices, the RSMK calculates the smoothed change in the natural logarithm of the ratio and scales it as a percentage. # Auto Chart Patterns [Trendoscope®]

Version: 1.0.0. Delta: individual explanation of the complete saved publication.

**Classification:** indicator. Native publication type: study. Review: independently reviewed.

## Idea and objective

Automatically identify multiscale chart patterns as pairs of nonintersecting trendlines, then label their geometry, direction and expansion behavior.

## Coin-test readiness: incomplete

No complete standalone coin-test contract or runnable coin-test implementation has been qualified for this card. Source disclosure alone does not establish that readiness.

## Source calculation and gaps

**Disclosed principal calculation.** Usable for thirteen-case supplied-line classification with caller tolerances; automatic zigzag/line discovery remains outside scope.

No blocking gap was identified for the principal computation described above. Runtime integration and performance remain separate questions.

## How it works

- For supplied line pairs and caller flat/parallel tolerances, thirteen cases are: both rising/parallel = ascending channel; both falling/parallel = descending channel; both flat = ranging channel. Both rising and widening/narrowing = expanding/contracting rising wedge; both falling and widening/narrowing = expanding/contracting falling wedge. Upper rising/lower flat = expanding ascending triangle; upper flat/lower rising = contracting ascending triangle; upper flat/lower falling = expanding descending triangle; upper falling/lower flat = contracting descending triangle. Upper falling/lower rising = converging triangle; upper rising/lower falling = diverging triangle.
- Generate recursive zigzags from several length/depth combinations and inspect the latest five/six pivots. Require an upper line touching highs, a lower touching lows and no intervening candle outside them. Classify relative slopes as channels,wedges or triangles and converging,diverging or parallel.

## Outputs and intended use

- Draw the accepted pattern and alert on new detections. Rising/falling channels,wedge variants,ascending/descending triangles and bidirectional triangles are geometric descriptions, not complete trades or validated reversal probabilities.

## Parameters and stated settings

- Configure base zigzags,pivot count,error/flat thresholds,last-pivot direction,bar-ratio filtering,overlap policy and group/individual pattern toggles. Avoid Overlap ignores a candidate starting inside an existing pattern; numerical defaults are absent.

## Failure modes and caveats

- Multiple scales generate correlated structures and flexible tolerances can overfit visual history. Latest zigzag pivots may change before confirmation; a valid pattern is not a guaranteed breakout or prescribed direction.

## Missing information and implementation boundary

- Base/recursive swing algorithm, exact trendline fit/touch tolerance,error/flat units,bar-ratio limit and candle containment price definition are omitted.

## Data requirements

Required inputs: ohlcv.

Repository input-class support: available. OHLCV supports geometric pattern scanning; missing detection equations are algorithm gaps.

## Idea and objective

Realtime Delta Volume Action builds a custom live candle view from incoming price/volume updates. It supplements price action with signed update counts, signed volume, relative deltas and a volume-weighted update-price reference. The author emphasizes that the accumulated detail cannot be reconstructed from historical bars and disappears on reload, so this is live observational tooling rather than a replayable historical signal model.

## How it works

- Assign each feed update a sign from its price change, carrying the last sign through unchanged prices; accumulate signed tick and volume deltas per bar.
- Compute delta shares of totals and a volume-weighted mean of update prices, labeled POC by the author.
- Combine configurable marker conditions with AND logic; use DV polarity/intensity and candle disagreement for body colors and strong-bar borders.
- From ordered update prices assign+1 to increases,-1 to decreases, retaining last sign on unchanged prices. Within each bar DT=sum(sign),T=count(updates),DT%=100*DT/T for T>0. Initial polarity is caller-defined. Volume differencing and strong-bar extras remain unqualified.

## Outputs and intended use

- Inspect live bars and elapsed-live values, configure directional markers and alerts, and compare volume/tick evidence with price and a broader trend context.
- Usable scope: Live update-count delta/share. Other advertised outputs remain subject to the listed missing information.

- Reload/input changes erase accumulated observations; runtime/chart slowdown is disclosed. Analytical: price-change attribution is not actual buyer/seller aggressor data and the POC is a weighted mean rather than a modal price.

Version: 1.0.0. Delta: individual explanation of the complete saved publication.

- Yang-Zhang estimator details, radius conversion in log space, contact tolerances and sigmoid weights/calibration are undisclosed.

## How it works

- Estimate per-bar Yang-Zhang volatility, scale log-price by that estimate, then select two backward-scanned range-expansion candles and optionally the largest-range candle in a period.
- Each selected candle provides an outer full-range circle plus upper/lower wick circles. Standard/curtate cycloids use a shared outer rolling radius, traced-point radius and apex phase; numerical inversion maps each bar coordinate to an angle and exponential transformation restores price.
- Contact analysis combines contact direction, curve/zone, relative volume, delta, absorption and confluence through sigmoid scoring. Footprint mode compares contact-price rows; geometric/intrabar volume engines supply reduced alternatives.

## Outputs and intended use

- Polyline curves, apex/trough references, nearest support/resistance and a dashboard show geometry and contact behavior.
- P(up), conviction and behavior labels are heuristic outputs, not demonstrated calibrated probabilities.

- Volatility lookback default20, range1–2500; largest-candle lookback default20, range5–200.
- Live/closed calculation basis, trace/reference toggles, geometric/intrabar volume mode, recommended15-second intrabars and dashboard controls.

- Diffusion scaling assumes a model and does not prove geometric invariance or predictive causality across instruments.
- The source inconsistently describes fallback as geometry-only versus volume-engine data; footprint access and tick-level precision claims are not verified.

## Idea and objective

Correlation Heatmap compares aligned weekly or monthly arithmetic returns across a selected asset list. It aims to support diversification and relationship research while avoiding misleading comparisons caused by different session closing times. The distinctive alignment method reconstructs each other symbol’s price from sum/difference spread series sampled in chart context. - Chart interval must be at most monthly; requests include extended hours/dividend adjustments and inherited settlement settings.

# Markov Chain [3D] | Fractalyst

Version: 1.0.0. Delta: individual explanation of the complete saved publication.

**Classification:** indicator. Native publication type: study. Review: independently reviewed.

## Idea and objective

Markov Chain [3D] summarizes recent transitions among detected bullish, bearish and neutral regimes. Its animated state diagram is paired with a numeric bias output intended for connecting regime filters to separately specified systematic trading rules.

## Coin-test readiness: incomplete

No complete standalone coin-test contract or runnable coin-test implementation has been qualified for this card. Source disclosure alone does not establish that readiness.

## Source calculation and gaps

**Partly disclosed computation.** The detected-state-to-bias mapping is explicit, but the core regime boundaries, normalization/smoothing and transition pseudocount remain undisclosed.

- Define normalized regime boundaries, price-return transform, normalization/smoothing and Laplace pseudocount.

## How it works

- Export detected Bull as +1, Neutral as 0 and Bear as -1. This is direct state encoding; transition-probability estimates visualize the observed transition history and are not specified as selecting that bias.
- The engine standardizes price returns or three equally weighted custom series with rolling Z-scores, classifies normalized values into market states and smooths combined custom classifications. On confirmed bars it counts transitions in a rolling matrix and applies Laplace smoothing to estimate conditional next-state probabilities.
- Spheres represent states, self-loops persistence and directed arrows state changes. The description also contains an extensive separate feature-export script: centered oscillators, moving-average displacement, directional comparisons, volume transforms and range/return volatility are plotted for selection as inputs. That code does not supply the Markov classification algorithm itself.

## Outputs and intended use

- Bias is +1 bullish, zero neutral and -1 bearish. A sample consumer enters long when bias equals one and closes otherwise. Probability arrows describe observed conditional transitions, while bias alone exports a hard state rather than the complete probability vector.

## Parameters and stated settings

- Lookback defaults to 100 and controls both detection and probability history. Custom mode accepts three selected series with equal weights. The included exporter defines common lengths 14, 20 and 50, and produces 52 numbered plots despite surrounding 45-plus branding.

## Failure modes and caveats

- Estimated transition frequencies can shift across regimes and do not guarantee the next state. Confirmed-bar updates are an author claim, not an independently verified non-repainting guarantee. Several exporter names do not match conventional definitions: its MAMA is an ordinary EMA and its Klinger is a difference of smoothed price-times-volume.

## Missing information and implementation boundary

- Regime Z-score thresholds, adaptive normalization, price-return convention, combined-state smoothing and Laplace pseudocount are undisclosed. Exported bias is explicitly the detected regime label; no transition-probability-to-bias algorithm is claimed.

## Data requirements

Required inputs: ohlcv, optional caller-selected indicator series.

Repository input-class support: available. Default price-return mode and the supplied technical-feature exporter use OHLCV. Arbitrary custom sources require their own separately specified data contracts.

# Interactive Motive Wave Checklist

Version: 1.0.0. Delta: individual explanation of the complete saved publication.

**Classification:** analysis-tool. Native publication type: study. Review: independently reviewed.

## Idea and objective

Interactive Motive Wave Checklist tests a manually selected price structure against disclosed Elliott-wave-style conditions. It is an educational validation aid: the user supplies the candidate rather than an automatic market scanner discovering it. The checklist distinguishes general motive requirements from impulse and expanding/contracting diagonal constraints. Its results express consistency with the stated geometry and do not establish a price forecast.

## Coin-test readiness: incomplete

No complete standalone coin-test contract or runnable coin-test implementation has been qualified for this card. Source disclosure alone does not establish that readiness.

## Source calculation and gaps

**Disclosed principal calculation.** Usable for individual generic-motive and expanding/contracting diagonal checks on six supplied ordered pivots. The impulse extension rule and equality/boundary parity are not claimed.

No blocking gap was identified for the principal computation described above. Runtime integration and performance remain separate questions.

## How it works

- Narrow generic-motive/diagonal checklist: take six chronologically increasing pivot points P0…P5 with alternating high/low direction, and wave lengths L_i=abs(P_i−P_(i−1)). With direction d=sign(P1−P0), require L2<L1, d×(P3−P1)>0 and (L3>L1 or L3>L5), following the source strict bigger-than wording. For diagonals additionally require L4<L3 and P4 strictly inside the P0-to-P1 price territory. Contracting requires L1>L3>L5 and L2>L4; expanding requires L1<L3<L5 and L2<L4.
- Require chronologically ordered alternating pivots, limit second-wave retracement and require the third wave to exceed the first endpoint without being the shortest action wave.
- For impulses prohibit overlap of the first and fourth waves and test extension constraints.
- For diagonals restrict fourth-wave retracement, require overlap with first-wave territory and compare sequential action/correction magnitudes for expansion or contraction.

## Outputs and intended use

- After selecting the points, inspect pass/fail checklist items on the chart.
- Use the result to learn how candidate impulse/diagonal structures differ.

## Parameters and stated settings

- Six pivots define the candidate. Retracement rules use 100% and extension is defined above 200%.
- User selects six timestamped price pivots; no automatic pivot detection is needed. Strict inequalities define the narrow checklist; complete impulse validity and extension>200% denominator remain outside scope.

## Failure modes and caveats

- Manual candidate selection introduces hindsight and interpretation bias.
- The phrase all not extended is ambiguous about whether every action wave is individually prohibited from extension.

## Missing information and implementation boundary

- Extension-ratio denominator and its exact aggregate impulse condition are unclear; equality cases are not fully specified.

# Time-of-Day/Session Performance Stats [QuantAlgo]

Version: 1.0.0. Delta: individual explanation of the complete saved publication.

**Classification:** analysis-tool. Native publication type: study. Review: independently reviewed.

## Idea and objective

Time-of-Day/Session Performance Stats ranks historical activity by hour and session to help traders focus on appropriate market windows. It separately measures range, volume, directional frequency and average open-to-close drift, avoiding the assumption that a high bullish bar count necessarily means positive average return. Session overlaps count in every involved session. The focus-hour plans are allocations of attention derived from rankings, not verified portfolio weights or a complete trading system. The author claims trailing-window overlays avoid repainting, but that implementation behavior is not independently established here.

## Coin-test readiness: incomplete

No complete standalone coin-test contract or runnable coin-test implementation has been qualified for this card. Source disclosure alone does not establish that readiness.

## Source calculation and gaps

**Disclosed principal calculation.** Usable for raw-range Activity, mean Volume, directional-bar Bias and mean open-to-close Drift by chosen hour/session buckets, plus their individual rankings. Aggregated edge/percentile ties, focus allocations and overlay timing remain outside this scope.

No blocking gap was identified for the principal computation described above. Runtime integration and performance remain separate questions.

## How it works

- Assign usable historical bars to local-hour and enabled-session buckets under lookback/max-bar limits.
- Narrow ordinary statistics: for each local-hour/session bucket, average raw High−Low bar range for Activity and average bar volume for Volume. Bias=100×count(Close>Open)/(count(Close>Open)+count(Close<Open)), excluding flat bars. Drift is the mean open-to-close percentage change, 100×(Close−Open)/Open. Rank individual Activity/Volume/Bias/Drift boards by their respective values, and sessions by mean raw range per bar; equal-score ordering is unspecified.
- Average range/volume, exclude flat bars from bullish share, calculate mean percentage drift and combine percentile ranks into an aggregate.
- Discard underpopulated hours and rank sessions by average range per bar.

## Outputs and intended use

- Five ranking boards, session/focus panels, historical overlays and hour/session-transition alerts support scheduling research.

## Parameters and stated settings

- Four sessions and 24 hours; five boards. Mix top-two uses 80/20, conservative top-three 50/30/20; aggressive top-one and avoid lowest-range hour.
- Timezone, windows, weekday filtering, inclusion mode, minimum count and lookback are adjustable.
- Above one-hour chart interval warns of missing buckets; examples recommend 5/15/30m or 1H.
- Choose raw-price range mode to avoid the optional percent-of-close range convention. Caller supplies lookback days, hard bar ceiling, minimum bucket count, timezone, enabled sessions/custom HHMM-HHMM windows and bar/weekday inclusion settings; no numeric defaults for these are supplied.

## Failure modes and caveats

- Aggregated directional-edge definition is absent and can change rankings.
- Timezone/DST, partial bars and overlapping sessions affect samples.
- Historical rank leadership does not guarantee future activity or profitability.

## Missing information and implementation boundary

- Exact range-percentage denominator timing, edge formula, percentile ties, lookback defaults and overlay update cutoff are absent.

## Data requirements

# ATR Rope

Version: 1.0.0. Delta: individual explanation of the complete saved publication.

**Classification:** indicator. Native publication type: study. Review: independently reviewed.

## Idea and objective

Separate movement beyond an ATR-sized tolerance from smaller noise and preserve reference zones formed while the filtered center stays flat.

## Coin-test readiness: incomplete

No complete standalone coin-test contract or runnable coin-test implementation has been qualified for this card. Source disclosure alone does not establish that readiness.

## Source calculation and gaps

**Disclosed principal calculation.** Usable for the excess-distance rope-center recurrence with caller-supplied ATR tolerance, source and starting rope; exact published initialization and consolidation-zone lifecycle remain outside scope.

No blocking gap was identified for the principal computation described above. Runtime integration and performance remain separate questions.

## How it works

- For selected source S, previous rope R and supplied ATR tolerance A, leave R fixed while S is within [R-A,R+A]. When S exceeds the upper boundary, shift R upward by S-(R+A); below the lower boundary, shift it down by (R-A)-S. Thus the rope moves only by the distance beyond its tolerance envelope.
- Color upward rope motion green and downward motion red; a source crossing of the rope turns it blue/flat. Optional channel bounds are rope plus/minus ATR. During flat areas the upper/lower observations are accumulated and averaged into consolidation zones, whose exact lifecycle is not fully specified.

## Outputs and intended use

- Use rope, optional ATR bounds and extending zones to interpret trends, consolidation and retests. The author explicitly says it supplies no complete signal system.

## Parameters and stated settings

- Source is caller-selected, illustrated by separate high/low instances. ATR channel is hidden by default. The narrow recurrence accepts a supplied ATR series and initial rope value; published ATR length/estimator and seed defaults are not specified.

## Failure modes and caveats

- The source claims live-drawn zones do not repaint, but unavailable code prevents verification. ATR changes and developing bars can shift boundaries; visual retests do not define executable setups.

# Delta Volume Channels [LucF]

Version: 1.0.0. Delta: individual explanation of the complete saved publication.

**Classification:** analysis-tool. Native publication type: study. Review: independently reviewed.

## Idea and objective

Translate lower-timeframe directional-volume estimates into price-chart channels and configurable condition markers. The design emphasizes visual pressure and consolidation context rather than raw flow values or verified exchange aggressor volume.

## Coin-test readiness: incomplete

No complete standalone coin-test contract or runnable coin-test implementation has been qualified for this card. Source disclosure alone does not establish that readiness.

## Source calculation and gaps

**Disclosed principal calculation.** Intrabar DV/DVpercent is independently defined by the disclosed procedure; other missing outputs do not qualify.

No blocking gap was identified for the principal computation described above. Runtime integration and performance remain separate questions.

## How it works

- Classify intrabar volume by open/close direction, then prior-close change for flat bars, then last polarity. Summed up minus down volume forms delta; dividing by total intrabar volume gives delta percentage.
- A reference average and an average of a delta/relative-volume-weighted source define a channel. Their ordering sets bull/bear state; source-close position and both slopes strengthen that state.
- A divergence means disagreement of the two average slopes. Save divergence-bar levels, expand them on later divergences until breached, and reset with a new divergence after breach. Channel breakout direction combines with pressure strength for stronger states.
- Sign intrabar volume by close-open;flat body uses close-previous_intrabar_close;unchanged price carries last polarity. Sum U,D;DV=U-D;DV%=100*(U-D)/(U+D) for positive total. Caller supplies LTF/initial polarity and adequate observations. Weighted source/channels and marker filters remain outside scope.

## Outputs and intended use

- Filled channels, bar colors, divergence marks and optional raw-value tooltips support discretionary stop tightening or confirmation.
- Markers/alerts use caller-selected state transitions and filters at bar close. The author’s non-repaint claim is limited to that timing and is not independently verified.
- Usable scope: Intrabar DV/DVpercent. Other advertised outputs remain subject to the listed missing information.

## Parameters and stated settings

- Default reference is close ALMA length20, weighted line capped at five reference standard deviations.
- Divergence defaults use high/low boundaries; upside breach requires low above top and downside high below bottom. Precision, MA type/source/length, cap, volume weighting and marker filters are configurable.

## Failure modes and caveats

- Lower-timeframe polarity is a flow proxy; data coverage and volume-reporting quality constrain interpretation.
- Channel colors do not encode a complete trade policy; a weakened strong state need not predict reversal.

## Missing information and implementation boundary

- Exact relative-volume normalization, weighted-price transformation, cap lookback and complete marker-filter definitions are omitted.

**Classification:** analysis-tool. Native publication type: study. Review: independently reviewed.

## Idea and objective

Volume Delta Compare contrasts live-update and lower-timeframe estimates of directional volume. Its purpose is to show why the same chart candle can yield different delta values depending on observation granularity. It preserves a neutral category instead of forcing unchanged-price volume into a directional side. The outputs describe price-direction-classified volume rather than verified exchange aggressor flow, and the live path loses accumulated information when re-executed.

## Coin-test readiness: incomplete

No complete standalone coin-test contract or runnable coin-test implementation has been qualified for this card. Source disclosure alone does not establish that readiness.

## Source calculation and gaps

**Disclosed principal calculation.** The directional allocation and delta computation are explicitly defined.

No blocking gap was identified for the principal computation described above. Runtime integration and performance remain separate questions.

## How it works

- Assign incremental live volume to up, down or neutral according to the direction of the observed price change.
- For the lower-timeframe path assign each sub-bar volume by its price movement, which can disagree with the intrabar sequence.
- Subtract down from up volume for delta and sum delta for cumulative delta; compare candle direction with delta sign for divergence colors.

## Outputs and intended use

- View category columns, delta stepline, cumulative-only view and per-bar/tick details.
- Choose whether live calculation begins immediately on a partially formed bar or waits for a fresh bar.

## Idea and objective

Trend Type Indicator categorizes price behavior as sideways, upward or downward using volatility and directional-movement tools. It is intended for comparing trend context across chart timeframes before applying a separate trend-trading method. The publication distinguishes strength/range detection from direction, which avoids assuming that high volatility alone means an uptrend. No blocking gap was identified for the principal computation described above. Runtime integration and performance remain separate questions.

## How it works

- Narrow raw ADX-only classifier: disable the ATR sideways filter, enable ADX with chosen DI length and ADX smoothing. ADX≤25 means sideways; otherwise +DI>−DI means uptrend and −DI>+DI means downtrend. Equal DI above the threshold remains unspecified. This is the pre-display classification, not the published smoothed/lagged oscillator.
- Classify sideways conditions when ATR is below its moving average or ADX indicates insufficient trend strength, according to enabled filters.
- For non-sideways conditions compare positive and negative directional indicators for upward versus downward direction.
- Apply configurable smoothing and lag to the displayed oscillator/status.

- Check agreement across higher and lower chart timeframes as contextual confirmation.

- ATR/DI lengths, average type, smoothing factor and lag are configurable.
- Use ADX threshold25 with caller-selected DI and ADX smoothing lengths; do not infer numeric defaults for these. Both-filter combination, output smoothing and default eight-bar lag are outside narrow scope.

- Low ATR and low ADX measure different properties and may disagree.

# Smart Trader, Episode 06, Isotropic Trend Lines

Version: 1.0.0. Delta: individual explanation of the complete saved publication.

**Classification:** analysis-tool. Native publication type: study. Review: independently reviewed.

## Idea and objective

Isotropic Trend Lines measures structural trend slope in log-price units normalized by realized volatility, aiming to make steepness less dependent on display scaling. It reduces non-overlapping blocks to range midpoints, finds a monotonic sequence, fits boundary lines through selected extremes and compares multiple scales. A state machine describes channel exits, returns and failures. This is contextual channel analysis rather than buy/sell advice. Volatility normalization helps comparability but cannot make different sampling intervals economically identical or make correlated prime-length analyses independent.

## Coin-test readiness: incomplete

No complete standalone coin-test contract or runnable coin-test implementation has been qualified for this card. Source disclosure alone does not establish that readiness.

## Source calculation and gaps

**Partly disclosed computation.** Core source rules need the listed gaps resolved.

- Primary-scale/default conflict and incomplete volatility/state-transition equations prevent exact reproduction.

## How it works

- Estimate Yang-Zhang sigma; form each block’s geometric high/low midpoint.
- Find longest recent same-direction midpoint chain and compute arctangent(log displacement/sigma/elapsed bars).
- Fit log-linear upper/lower boundaries through extreme highs/lows, aggregate scale directions and track sigma-distance break/retest states.

## Outputs and intended use

- Channel/projection/fill, endpoint markers, trend-angle label and narrative dashboard support structural context.

## Parameters and stated settings

- Six stated scales 3,7,13,19,29,47, with primary user period; later defaults say period26/groups5/sigma20, conflicting with repeated scale19 wording.
- One-sigma excursion/rebound defines retest/confirmation context; consensus examples 5/6,6/6 and range≥4/6.
- Live default updates intrabar; Close mode shifts one bar and suppresses all nineteen alerts.

## Failure modes and caveats

- Primary-scale/default inconsistency affects reproduction.
- Live mode repaints intrabar; Close mode retains a deliberately live price header.
- Yang-Zhang assumptions and channel-extreme ordering can fail in unusual data.

## Missing information and implementation boundary

- Exact sigma equations/weights, state transition thresholds, boundary degeneracy handling and range-threshold default are absent.

# RSI Impact Heat Map [Trendoscope]

Version: 1.0.0. Delta: individual explanation of the complete saved publication.

**Classification:** analysis-tool. Native publication type: study. Review: independently reviewed.

## Idea and objective

Evaluate the subsequent upside and downside excursion associated with a selected RSI crossing event using a two-dimensional outcome heatmap.

## Coin-test readiness: incomplete

No complete standalone coin-test contract or runnable coin-test implementation has been qualified for this card. Source disclosure alone does not establish that readiness.

## Source calculation and gaps

**Disclosed principal calculation.** Usable for percent-mode post-crossing excursion pairs with caller-selected RSI settings, threshold, direction and N; ATR mode and exact heatmap parity remain outside scope.

No blocking gap was identified for the principal computation described above. Runtime integration and performance remain separate questions.

## How it works

- Choose an RSI series/length, crossing direction, threshold and future horizon N. A crossover/crossunder through that threshold creates an event at close C. In percentage mode, record the highest upward and lowest downward displacement from C over the subsequent N bars, scaled by 100/C, as that event’s outcome pair.
- Store each completed pair separately. Optional ATR scaling and a percentile-trimmed two-dimensional heatmap visualize the outcome distribution, but their exact ATR reference, clipping and color equations are not specified.

## Outputs and intended use

- Quadrants distinguish two-sided volatility, predominantly bearish outcomes, small moves and predominantly bullish outcomes. This is conditional historical excursion research, not a live prediction of a completed outcome.

## Parameters and stated settings

- Event threshold/direction, horizon, scaling and outlier range are configurable. Grid size ranges ten to ninety and defaults fifty, described as 51 by 51 cells.

## Failure modes and caveats

- Overlapping event windows are dependent. Outcome collection needs future bars, and percentile clipping can hide tail risks if the chart is interpreted without its settings.

## Missing information and implementation boundary

- Exact default RSI settings, equality/boundary conventions for the future horizon, ATR reference bar, percentile cutoff and color normalization are absent. Caller-selected RSI settings and percent-mode excursions are reproducible independently of those display/ATR details.

## Idea and objective

RedK Multi-Modal TrailingStop places several common stop-distance models behind one visual and alert interface. It aims to support management of an existing position, letting the trader change the stop method without changing how proximity and risk states are presented. A separate ATR-based distance gauge labels price as safe, watch or critical regardless of the selected stop model. The introductory claim of realizing maximum profit is aspirational: no trailing stop guarantees that outcome, and the indicator itself does not execute a broker order.

## How it works

- Select ATR/Supertrend, Chandelier, Donchian, standard-deviation channel or fixed-percentage trail.
- Feed the selected trail into common flip/cross logic and calculate price-to-stop distance in separate ATR units.
- Classify proximity into safe/watch/critical states and expose corresponding alerts.

## Outputs and intended use

- Stop line/bands, live method/side/price panel, zone-transition prices, flip/cross/critical alerts and screener flip value support risk monitoring.

## Parameters and stated settings

- Five methods and five alerts. Separate safe-zone ATR and method settings plus layout/colors are configurable.

## Idea and objective

Cup & Handle searches for paired pivot highs whose intervening closes remain below a temporary connecting line, then fits a cup-shaped envelope and a handle region. The detector tolerates a configurable fraction of bars breaking its upper/lower cup boundaries. Only the latest full drawing remains, while optional labels preserve historical locations for replay. # Adaptive Volume Delta Map

**Classification:** indicator. Native publication type: study. Review: independently reviewed.

## Idea and objective

Adaptive Volume Delta Map chooses available data granularity and displays directional-volume imbalance plus an optional per-price distribution. It aims to adapt an order-flow-style view to feed/subscription capabilities, from fine updates to coarse candles. The source advertises bid/ask midpoint classification, but it does not disclose the exact classification algorithm or distinguish actual exchange prints from estimates. Its overload safeguard disables the distribution when too many levels appear. This is a monitoring visualization, not an execution engine or a proven microstructure reconstruction.

- Aggregate delta into candles and optionally group buy/sell volume by tick-sized price rows.
- Disable the map when its price-level count exceeds a fixed threshold.

## Outputs and intended use

- Delta candles and price-level distribution support imbalance, absorption and divergence research.

## Parameters and stated settings

- Tick/seconds permissions, bid/ask-calculated mode, distribution visibility, Ticks Per Row and Calculated Bars are configurable.
- Automatic map disable threshold is above fifty levels.
